newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly up.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly up.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Wednesday issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing prices and are annual percentage rates.
The central bank does not post volumes.
Traders said the rates moved in narrow ranges in sluggish trading on expectations that the central bank would cut bank reserve ratios in the short term due to falling inflation.

The State Statistical Bureau said on Tuesday that retail price inflation fell to a year-on-year 4.7 percent in October from 5.00 percent in September and against a year-on-year 14.8 percent for the whole of 1995.
State banks and securities houses were net lenders and the short-term financial centres, money brokerages run by the central bank, were major borrowers, traders said.

"There is sufficient money supply at the national level with banks and securities houses continuing to lend out money," one trader said. "But expectations of the bank reserve ratio cut prevented the rates from rising sharply."
"The major demand came from Guangdong and Anhui. Beijing and Shanghai were the biggest suppliers," said another trader.
Traders expect the rates to continue to move in a narrow range in the next few days.
